title: Kitchen chemistry
examples: What happens when I mix baking soda and vinegar?
Is dissolving always a chemical change?
Can you give me an example of a physical change?

explain.say: Today we explore chemistry in your own kitchen.

items: It is fun to learn about.

explain.say: First we look at baking soda and vinegar together.
The mix creates a gas called carbon dioxide.
Next we learn about dissolving things in water.
Now we compare physical and chemical changes.
When you bake a cake, the ingredients change chemically.

faq.q: Does everything that changes have to be a chemical change?
faq.a: No, many changes are physical changes. For example, tearing paper is just a physical change.
asks: Is cutting wood a chemical change?
What is the difference between physical and chemical?

faq.q: What is the difference between dissolving and a chemical reaction?
faq.a: Dissolving is usually physical because you can often get the original substance back. A chemical reaction makes something brand new.
asks: If I mix sugar in tea, is that chemical?

faq.q: Is the gas from vinegar and baking soda a chemical change?
faq.a: Yes, the formation of a new gas is evidence of a chemical change happening. You made something new.
asks: Does gas production mean a reaction?

faq.q: If I freeze water, is that a chemical change?
faq.a: No, freezing water is only a physical change. The substance is still just water, just in a different state.

faq.q: What does 'dissolving' mean in chemistry terms?
faq.a: It means one substance, the solute, mixes evenly into another, the solvent. The solute spreads out completely.
asks: What is the solvent in salt water?

facts: A chemical change creates a substance with different properties.
A physical change alters the form but not the chemical identity.
When baking soda and vinegar mix, they produce carbon dioxide gas.
Dissolving is a physical change because the solute can often be recovered.

quiz.say: When you boil water into steam, is this a chemical change?
quiz.why: Boiling is only a change of state, which is a physical change.

wrong.0: This is tempting because gas production suggests a reaction.
wrong.1: This is tempting because heat is often associated with chemical reactions.
wrong.3: This is tempting because it involves a dramatic change in appearance.

quiz.say: If you leave salt in water until it evaporates, what type of change occurred?
quiz.why: The salt remains salt, it just becomes visible again after the water leaves.

wrong.0: This is tempting because the water seems to break down.
wrong.2: This is tempting because something seems to disappear from the solution.
wrong.3: This is tempting because the process involves heat and change.

quiz.say: What is the gas produced when baking soda and vinegar mix?
quiz.why: The specific reaction between these two chemicals always produces this gas.

wrong.0: This is tempting because it is another carbon-containing gas.
wrong.2: This is tempting because oxygen is a common gas we learn about.
wrong.3: This is tempting because water is involved in the mixture.
